query: Along the ~200 km receiver-function profile across the Red Sea rift in the Afar Depression, crustal thickness averages about 22 ± 4 km and varies from approximately 17 km beneath the Tendaho graben axis to 30 km in the northeastern overlap zone, with an asymmetric pattern of gradual thickening southwest of the rift flank and sharper thickening northeastward in the overlap zone.
